record.original_question: Can one define a mathematically robust category of wild virtual knots, formulate its axioms, and prove a theorem describing when a wild equivalence between tame virtual links implies a tame equivalence between those links?

evidence.quote: Create the category of 'wild virtual knots' and establish its axiomatics. In particular, one needs a theorem that states when a wild equivalence of tame virtual links implies a tame equivalence of these links.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A virtual link diagram is a 4-valent planar graph whose vertices are decorated as either classical crossings (over/under information) or virtual crossings (marked with a small circle). Two virtual link diagrams are called tame-equivalent if one can be transformed into the other by a finite sequence of classical Reidemeister moves and the virtual Reidemeister moves (the detour move). A virtual link is the tame-equivalence class of a virtual link diagram.

By analogy with classical knot theory, one may consider "wild" virtual knots — virtual analogues of wild knots, obtained for instance as limits of infinite sequences of local tangle replacements, or as continuous images of S^1 in a suitable ambient setting that admit virtual-crossing information but are not equivalent to any finite virtual diagram. Two wild virtual objects can be related by a notion of "wild equivalence" extending the tame Reidemeister/detour moves to allow such limiting processes.

The problem is the following:

(a) Give a precise mathematical definition of the category of wild virtual knots: specify its objects, its morphisms, and the equivalence relation that determines isomorphism, together with a complete set of axioms.

(b) Within this framework, prove a theorem characterizing when wild equivalence of two tame virtual links implies their tame equivalence. That is, identify necessary and sufficient conditions under which two tame virtual links that become equivalent in the wild category are already equivalent as tame virtual links.
artifact.status_search_result: This problem appears in published lists of unsolved problems in virtual knot theory (e.g., a 2014 compilation of open problems in virtual knot theory), and no construction of a fully axiomatized category of wild virtual knots together with the desired tame-vs-wild equivalence theorem appears in the literature. The status appears to be open.

status_evidence.title: Unsolved Problems in Virtual Knot Theory and Combinatorial Knot Theory
status_evidence.snippet: List of open problems in virtual knot theory including questions about wild virtual knots and their axiomatics.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of building a category of wild virtual knots with appropriate axiomatics is listed among the unsolved problems in virtual knot theory.

status_evidence.title: Wild Knots are Wildly Difficult to Classify — The n-Category Café
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of recent results indicating that wild knots are extremely difficult to classify.
status_evidence.claim: Classification of wild knots, even in the classical setting, remains an active and largely open research area, suggesting the virtual analogue is also open.
